ovarian clear cell carcinoma: Clear or eosinophilic hobnail cells with distinct borders and atypical nuclei.
Ovarian clear cell carcinoma with tubulocystic, papillary, or solid architecture and hyalinized stromal cores.
clear cell carcinoma of the ovary
ovarian endometrioid carcinoma: Columnar epithelial cells forming glands with variable squamous differentiation and nuclear atypia.
Ovarian endometrioid carcinoma with confluent glandular or cribriform architecture resembling endometrial glands.
ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma: High-grade serous carcinoma with complex papillary, solid, or slit-like architecture and destructive invasion.
Marked nuclear pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli, brisk mitotic activity, and frequent apoptotic bodies.
ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma: Low-grade serous carcinoma with orderly micropapillary architecture, delicate papillae, and relatively uniform growth.
Monomorphic nuclei with mild atypia, low mitotic activity, and possible psammoma bodies.
ovarian mucinous carcinoma: Ovarian mucinous carcinoma with expansile or infiltrative mucinous glands and complex intestinal-type architecture.
Tall mucin-rich columnar cells with stratification, atypia, and intracytoplasmic mucin.
